run_note: Heads up: today's update only covers 14 of the usual 15 holdings. Thermo Fisher Scientific wasn't scored because of a technical problem on our side — nothing to do with the company itself.

LHX.sentence: L3Harris ticked up slightly — its profit margins are running thinner than the bigger defense contractors right now, which is the real drag, but steady military spending means the underlying business is fine.

LIN.sentence: Linde is barely moving, which is exactly its character — it sells oxygen and nitrogen on long contracts, nudges prices up a little each quarter, and investors tend to hide in it when markets get jittery.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft is quiet and holding up far better than other big tech names — the Azure cloud and AI story keeps grinding along without any drama.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher Scientific didn't get scored in today's run because of a technical problem on our side — nothing happened to the company itself. It should be back in tomorrow's update.

CVX.sentence: Chevron is flat, and the thing to keep in mind is that today's high oil prices come from Middle East tensions disrupting Gulf shipments rather than anything Chevron did — the stock is actually priced around a normal, lower oil price, so it isn't banking on the war premium lasting.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow has fallen more than 40% from its high, which is a dramatic drop for a company this profitable — big companies and government agencies keep signing on for its workflow and AI-assistant tools, so this looks more like a market mood swing than a business problem.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore slipped a few percent even as copper prices jumped — odd for a copper miner, since the stock usually follows the metal, so it's lagging a move that would normally help it.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta dipped a bit, but the price it gets per ton of crushed stone is still creeping up — the headline price looked soft only because of the mix of products sold, and that's the number that actually matters with this quarry business.

KOF.sentence: Coca-Cola FEMSA eased back as the Mexican peso weakened, which quietly shrinks the value of its mostly-Mexican earnings when converted to dollars — a currency headwind rather than anything wrong with selling Coke across Latin America.

UBER.sentence: Uber was roughly flat, and the thing to watch is that people keep booking more rides and meals through the app — the robotaxi companies haven't visibly dented that yet, so the self-driving worry is still about the future, not today.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk dropped over 6% and now trades below what its fleet of container ships would cost to replace — for a shipping company that's historically been a sign it's gotten cheap, though shipping is famously tied to the ups and downs of global trade.

MA.sentence: Mastercard is essentially flat and, unusually, is priced slightly below its twin Visa — normally it trades at a premium — while people keep tapping their cards more than ever, so the business itself is humming along.

ISRG.sentence: The surgical-robot maker fell nearly 3% but is still down about a quarter from its highs — hospitals keep doing more procedures on its da Vinci machines, and every operation means more single-use supplies sold.

NVDA.sentence: Nvidia rose a bit, but the real question hanging over it is that two of its biggest customers — Google's parent and Amazon — are now spending more on computing gear than their businesses bring in and borrowing the rest, so whether those customers can keep paying is what matters, not anything about Nvidia's chips themselves.
